title: Marathas and Khalsa Panth 's Ransacking of (a City of Sirhind) Suba Asmand Khan was handed over to Ahmad Shah…

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Mughals who had once been emperors at Delhi, Somehow they kept themselves entrenched within the city. The Pathan chief Ahmed Shah Abdali from Kandhar1 , Held sovereignty over the areas surrounding Delhi. (1)
lines: As the Mughals who had once been emperors at Delhi,
Somehow they kept themselves entrenched within the city.
The Pathan chief Ahmed Shah Abdali from Kandhar1 ,
Held sovereignty over the areas surrounding Delhi.

blocks.text: As the Delhi residents came to hear about the news, That Buland Khan2 had runaway (from Lahore after being defeated), Ghazi-ud-din3 Gazdi sprang up from his hiding place. Taking Marhatta troops along with his own forces. (2)
lines: As the Delhi residents came to hear about the news,
That Buland Khan2 had runaway (from Lahore after being defeated),
Ghazi-ud-din3 Gazdi sprang up from his hiding place.
Taking Marhatta troops along with his own forces.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Paying a ransom of one lakh rupees to the supporting Marathas, He made the Marahatta forces march in the vanguard. As Samand Khan4 , the Sirhind chief had revolted against the Delhi ruler, The Maratha forces tried to settle scores with him. (3)
lines: Paying a ransom of one lakh rupees to the supporting Marathas,
He made the Marahatta forces march in the vanguard.
As Samand Khan4 , the Sirhind chief had revolted against the Delhi ruler,
The Maratha forces tried to settle scores with him.

blocks.text: As Samand Khan did not allow them to enter the city for many days, They lost their steam after fighting against him for many days. At this Dina Beg5 , the erstwhile minister, made a surmise, That Samand Khan could not be eliminated without Singhs' support. (4)
lines: As Samand Khan did not allow them to enter the city for many days,
They lost their steam after fighting against him for many days.
At this Dina Beg5 , the erstwhile minister, made a surmise,
That Samand Khan could not be eliminated without Singhs' support.

blocks.text: The minister suggested that a ransom be paid to the Singhs, In order to make them partners in the alliance against Samand Khan. Thereafter, Dina Beg sent Sadiq Beg as the Mughals' emissary to the Singhs, Who brought the Singhs for negotiations with the Mughals. (5)
lines: The minister suggested that a ransom be paid to the Singhs,
In order to make them partners in the alliance against Samand Khan.
Thereafter,
Dina Beg sent Sadiq Beg as the Mughals' emissary to the Singhs,
Who brought the Singhs for negotiations with the Mughals.

blocks.text: Refusing to accept any ransom for this expedition, The Singhs assured the Mughals to crush the city's Pathan6 forces. Seeking a guarantee for Singhs' ransacking the city of Sirhind, The Singhs promised to launch an instant attack on Sirhind. (6)
lines: Refusing to accept any ransom for this expedition,
The Singhs assured the Mughals to crush the city's Pathan6 forces.
Seeking a guarantee for Singhs' ransacking the city of Sirhind,
The Singhs promised to launch an instant attack on Sirhind.

blocks.text: Dohra:

A Lion in the j ungle can be killed in an instant, Provided the whole jungle is set on fire all around. An enemy fortification can be damaged instantly, Only when the entire surrounding area is ransacked. (7)
lines: A Lion in the j ungle can be killed in an instant,
Provided the whole jungle is set on fire all around.
An enemy fortification can be damaged instantly,
Only when the entire surrounding area is ransacked.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Khalsa Panth Singhs got a sanction for the city's ransacking, Making the Mughals take an oath on the holy Koran. Thereafter, setting up their base camp in the Punjabi garden, The Singhs launched an attack on the city of Sirhind. (8)
lines: The Khalsa Panth Singhs got a sanction for the city's ransacking,
Making the Mughals take an oath on the holy Koran.
Thereafter, setting up their base camp in the Punjabi garden,
The Singhs launched an attack on the city of Sirhind.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As had been ordained by the Divine Guru (Guru Gobind Singh7 ), The opportunity for the fulfillment of Guru's words arrived. It was an opportunity to commit plunder and arson, For which the Singhs had been waiting so passionately. (9)
lines: As had been ordained by the Divine Guru (Guru Gobind Singh7 ),
The opportunity for the fulfillment of Guru's words arrived.
It was an opportunity to commit plunder and arson,
For which the Singhs had been waiting so passionately.

blocks.text: Thus did the Singhs invade Sirhind as strongly, As had the brave Hanuman's monkey force invaded Sri Lanka. Thus did the Singhs climb up the Pathan forts' walls, That on-every projection were the Singhs seen sitting. (10)
lines: Thus did the Singhs invade Sirhind as strongly,
As had the brave Hanuman's monkey force invaded Sri Lanka.
Thus did the Singhs climb up the Pathan forts' walls,
That on-every projection were the Singhs seen sitting.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Singhs entered the fort after jumping over the walls, Did the Gilja Pathan troops take to their heals scared. Whosoever dared to fight was killed by the Singhs, Thus did the Durrani Pathan troops get defeated by the Singhs. (11)
lines: As the Singhs entered the fort after jumping over the walls,
Did the Gilja Pathan troops take to their heals scared.
Whosoever dared to fight was killed by the Singhs,
Thus did the Durrani Pathan troops get defeated by the Singhs.

blocks.text: Thereafter did the Singhs ransack and plunder the fort so thoroughly, That they carried all the valuables to their base camp. On the second day, as the Marathas also joined in the plunder, From all the sides, did the people join in loot and plunder. (12)
lines: Thereafter did the Singhs ransack and plunder the fort so thoroughly,
That they carried all the valuables to their base camp.
On the second day, as the Marathas also joined in the plunder,
From all the sides, did the people join in loot and plunder.

blocks.text: As there broke out a scuffle between the Singhs and Marathas, The Singhs decided to loot and plunder the Marathas as well. Thereafter, a thought crossed the Marathas's mind as well, That they must also loot the treasure from the Singh's base camp. (13)
lines: As there broke out a scuffle between the Singhs and Marathas,
The Singhs decided to loot and plunder the Marathas as well.
Thereafter, a thought crossed the Marathas's mind as well,
That they must also loot the treasure from the Singh's base camp.

blocks.text: As (majority) of the Singhs would enter the city for plundering, Only a handful of them would remain positioned in their camp. Then would the Marhattas invade the Singhs' base camp, Otherwise, the Singhs would certainly harass the Marhattas. (14)
lines: As (majority) of the Singhs would enter the city for plundering,
Only a handful of them would remain positioned in their camp.
Then would the Marhattas invade the Singhs' base camp,
Otherwise, the Singhs would certainly harass the Marhattas.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As Dina Beg came to hear these Maratha confabulations, He did convey the secret Maratha Plan to the Singhs. The pledge that Dina Beg had made to the Singhs, He felt he had fulfilled by leaking that news. (15)
lines: As Dina Beg came to hear these Maratha confabulations,
He did convey the secret Maratha Plan to the Singhs.
The pledge that Dina Beg had made to the Singhs,
He felt he had fulfilled by leaking that news.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Then did Dina Beg advise the Singhs to depart from there, Warning them to desist from entering into the city. To which did the Singhs pay heed as were they advised, Making a departure from their camp in the afternoon. (16)
lines: Then did Dina Beg advise the Singhs to depart from there,
Warning them to desist from entering into the city.
To which did the Singhs pay heed as were they advised,
Making a departure from their camp in the afternoon.

blocks.text: As the Marathas kept waiting for Singhs' entry into the city, They attacked the Singhs the moment the Singhs departed. As the Singhs had already chalked out their strategy, They had deliberately set the Marhattas on their trail. (17)
lines: As the Marathas kept waiting for Singhs' entry into the city,
They attacked the Singhs the moment the Singhs departed.
As the Singhs had already chalked out their strategy,
They had deliberately set the Marhattas on their trail.

blocks.text: As the Marathas kept chasing the Singhs for two miles, The horse mounted Singhs turned back to face the Marhattas. As the Singhs opened a volley of bullets on the chasing Marathas, They shot a majority of Maratha soldiers who were trailing them. (18)
lines: As the Marathas kept chasing the Singhs for two miles,
The horse mounted Singhs turned back to face the Marhattas.
As the Singhs opened a volley of bullets on the chasing Marathas,
They shot a majority of Maratha soldiers who were trailing them.

blocks.text: As the Marathas turned back shouting 'retreat' in their own dialect, The Singhs were too close to hit them behind their backs. Whichever Maratha soldier with a lance did the Singhs spot out, Instantly was he shot by the Singhs from a very close range. (19)
lines: As the Marathas turned back shouting 'retreat' in their own dialect,
The Singhs were too close to hit them behind their backs.
Whichever Maratha soldier with a lance did the Singhs spot out,
Instantly was he shot by the Singhs from a very close range.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whosoever among the Marathas chose to confront the Singhs, Him did the Singhs shoot and kill there and then. Then as the darkness of night descended on the scene, Did the harassed Marathas return to their camp. (20)
lines: Whosoever among the Marathas chose to confront the Singhs,
Him did the Singhs shoot and kill there and then.
Then as the darkness of night descended on the scene,
Did the harassed Marathas return to their camp.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Marathas proved to be an easy game for the Singh sharp shooters, The Singhs killed the Marathas as easily as a falcon kills the harassed quails. As the Singhs arrived in the Majha region to sort out things, They halted their horses on the outskirts of city of Lahore. (21)
lines: As the Marathas proved to be an easy game for the Singh sharp shooters,
The Singhs killed the Marathas as easily as a falcon kills the harassed quails.
As the Singhs arrived in the Majha region to sort out things,
They halted their horses on the outskirts of city of Lahore.

blocks.text: Thus had the Singhs ransacked and ruined the city of Sirhind, As Nawab Samand Khan8 had been defeated in the battle. The Marathas had not allowed him to escape on his horse. As they had intercepted him a few miles outside the city. (22)
lines: Thus had the Singhs ransacked and ruined the city of Sirhind,
As Nawab Samand Khan8 had been defeated in the battle.
The Marathas had not allowed him to escape on his horse.
As they had intercepted him a few miles outside the city.

blocks.text: Thereafter, as the Marathas stepped up their pressure on Lahore, The Singh forces too created chaotic conditions there. Then, as Taimur Shah9 marched towards the city of Lahore, He fled past Lahore on his way towards the city of Kabul. (23)
lines: Thereafter, as the Marathas stepped up their pressure on Lahore,
The Singh forces too created chaotic conditions there.
Then, as Taimur Shah9 marched towards the city of Lahore,
He fled past Lahore on his way towards the city of Kabul.

blocks.text: As both the cities of Lahore and Multan got vacated in panick, No Gilja Pathan could be spotted upto the banks of the river Attock. As the whole region fell into the hands of Singhs and Mughals, Marathas were the third contenders being under the service of the Mughals. (24)
lines: As both the cities of Lahore and Multan got vacated in panick,
No Gilja Pathan could be spotted upto the banks of the river Attock.
As the whole region fell into the hands of Singhs and Mughals,
Marathas were the third contenders being under the service of the Mughals.

blocks.text: Jhunkar Rao Holkar10 being the chief among the Maratha commanders, Tuka Rao, Ragho Rao and Malhar Rao Holkar were the other three commanders. The Singhs and Marathas being at loggerheads with each other, The Singhs kept dominating the Mughals as well as Marathas. (25)
lines: Jhunkar Rao Holkar10 being the chief among the Maratha commanders,
Tuka Rao,
Ragho Rao and Malhar Rao Holkar were the other three commanders.
The Singhs and Marathas being at loggerheads with each other,
The Singhs kept dominating the Mughals as well as Marathas.

blocks.text: As the Singhs started the construction of forts for themselves, They also started collecting revenues from the surrounding region. As the subdued Mughals felt scared of the Singhs' power, It was indeed a miracle of the Divine Guru's glorious blessings. (26)
lines: As the Singhs started the construction of forts for themselves,
They also started collecting revenues from the surrounding region.
As the subdued Mughals felt scared of the Singhs' power,
It was indeed a miracle of the Divine Guru's glorious blessings.

blocks.text: The Guru's grace had made sparrow-sized Singhs tear apart the falcon-sized Mughals, As he had made the rabbit-sized Singhs kill the lion-sized Mughals. Then had Mughals acknowledged the Singhs to be the most brave, As the Singhs had beaten and thrown out the mighty Pathans. (27)
lines: The Guru's grace had made sparrow-sized Singhs tear apart the falcon-sized Mughals,
As he had made the rabbit-sized Singhs kill the lion-sized Mughals.
Then had Mughals acknowledged the Singhs to be the most brave,
As the Singhs had beaten and thrown out the mighty Pathans.

blocks.text: It was for rendering this timely help to the Mughals against Pathans, That both Mughals and the Singhs developed fraternal regards for each other. As for the Marhattas, the Singhs did adopt a stern posture, So that they remained away from Singhs' direct line of offence. (28)
lines: It was for rendering this timely help to the Mughals against Pathans,
That both Mughals and the Singhs developed fraternal regards for each other.
As for the Marhattas, the Singhs did adopt a stern posture,
So that they remained away from Singhs' direct line of offence.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, laying a siege around the territory of Dina Beg, Did the Marathas take him into their captivity. It was the Maratha chief known by the name of Saba Patel11 , Who led the force which ransacked Dina Beg's territory. (29)
lines: Thereafter, laying a siege around the territory of Dina Beg,
Did the Marathas take him into their captivity.
It was the Maratha chief known by the name of Saba Patel11 ,
Who led the force which ransacked Dina Beg's territory.
